brightness-contrast-adjuster.quickAnswer: Upload a photo and move two sliders: brightness from -100 to +100 and contrast from -100 to +100. Each pixel is recalculated with the standard formula — output = (input - 128) x C + 128 + B. A pixel of 100 with brightness +20 and contrast +20 becomes 145. Reset anytime, download as PNG when it looks right.
keyFacts: Brightness shifts every pixel up or down by the same amount — like exposure compensation.
Contrast stretches or squeezes the distance of each pixel from mid-gray (128).
Both sliders run from -100 to +100 for fine, predictable control.
The math runs per pixel with the classic photo-editor formula, not a rough filter.
Adjustments apply to the original pixels every time — no quality stacking.
Reset returns the photo to its untouched original instantly.
howTo: Upload a photo (JPG, PNG, or WebP).
Raise brightness if the photo is dark; lower it if highlights are blown out.
Raise contrast if the photo looks flat and gray; lower it if shadows are crushed.
Watch the live preview — small moves of 10 to 20 usually suffice.
Click Reset to start over, or Download to save as PNG.
brightness-contrast-adjuster.formula:
C = 1 + (contrast / 100)      B = brightness x 2.55
output = (input - 128) x C + 128 + B
Result is clamped to 0..255 per channel.
brightness-contrast-adjuster.workedExample:
Pixel value 100, brightness +20, contrast +20:
1. C = 1 + 20/100 = 1.2.   B = 20 x 2.55 = 51.
2. Distance from mid-gray: 100 - 128 = -28.
3. Stretch: -28 x 1.2 = -33.6.
4. Re-center and shift: -33.6 + 128 + 51 = 145.4, rounded to 145.
5. The dark pixel brightens to 145 — lifted by brightness, pushed further from gray by contrast.
benefits: Rescue underexposed indoor shots and flat overcast photos in seconds.
Exact numeric control beats guessing with auto-enhance buttons.
Per-pixel math matches what desktop editors do — no surprises.
Non-destructive workflow: the original is reprocessed on every move.
Private editing with no uploads, accounts, or watermarks.
limitations: Cannot recover detail lost to pure black or pure white clipping.
Global adjustment only — no selective dodging, burning, or masks.
Extreme settings (+/-100) will posterize smooth gradients.
Heavy edits on JPGs can reveal compression artifacts.

faqs.q: What is the difference between brightness and contrast?
faqs.a: Brightness moves every pixel up or down equally — the whole image gets lighter or darker. Contrast changes the spread: it pushes bright pixels brighter and dark pixels darker (or squeezes them together at negative values). Dark photo? Brightness. Flat, gray photo? Contrast.

faqs.q: Will editing reduce my photo quality?
faqs.a: Each slider move reprocesses the original pixels, so quality never stacks up. One subtle risk: 8-bit rounding can band ultra-smooth gradients after extreme moves, but normal adjustments are visually lossless.

At +100, C = 2.0, so every pixel is pushed twice as far from mid-gray — most pixels slam into pure black or white. Real photos live in the +/-10 to +/-40 range. Extremes are there for artistic posterize effects.

faqs.q: Can I fix an overexposed photo?
faqs.a: Partly. Lowering brightness darkens the image, but pixels that clipped to pure white (255) contain no detail to recover — no editor can bring back what the sensor never recorded.

faqs.q: Does it work on transparent PNGs?
faqs.a: Yes — only the color channels are adjusted; the alpha (transparency) channel is left untouched.

faqs.q: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faqs.a: No. Every pixel is recalculated in your browser. Your photo never leaves your device.
